(2) Petitioner is resident of Village
Mostgaon, Udalgaon, District Bageshwar.
According to him, a motor road is proposed
to be constructed in the said village.
Petitioner submits that as per the proposed
alignment, part of his agricultural land
would be affected, therefore petitioner
submits that alignment of the road be
changed. Reliefs sought in the writ petition
are as follow:
"i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus, commanding and directing the
respondents not to construct the road as per the
present alignment of link road, connecting Baijnath-Bageshwar Motor Road to Udalgaon in absence of
public hearing and without obtaining 'no objection' of
the affected cultivators, including the petitioner.
ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing and commanding the
respondent authorities to conduct a fresh survey for
proposing an alignment around existing pathway of
the village so as to not to affect only one family in the
matter of acquisition of land and to construct a road
covering the land of different cultivators in equal
proportion."
(3) Learned State Counsel refers to
No Objection Certificate, issued by Gram
Pradhan, which is duly signed by the
villagers. He submits that petitioner has
also put his signature on the NOC at item
no. 16. Learned Counsel for the petitioner,
however, disputes the said submission and
submits that only name of the petitioner is

2025:UHC:9741
mentioned and petitioner has not put his
signature on the NOC.
(4) Be that as it may. Alignment of
motor road is decided by domain experts.
This is more so in hills where, due to
challenging topography and unique
geographical conditions, decision regarding
alignment has to be taken after several
rounds of survey. The domain experts have
taken a decision regarding points through
which the motor road would pass. Any
interference by this Court in the alignment
of the motor road will be counter-productive. The roads are lifeline of any
society. This is more so in the case of hills,
where, in the absence of roads, serious
patients are required to be carried for long
distances on foot in order to get them
treated.
(5) In view of the aforesaid, this
Court do not find any reason to interfere in
the matter. Writ petition thus fails and is
dismissed.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
